name: Hotel D'Angleterre Copenhagen
insider_take: This legendary palace hotel has been Copenhagen's crown jewel since 1755, hosting everyone from Hans Christian Andersen to Winston Churchill in its opulent halls overlooking Kongens Nytorv.
whats_special: The hotel sits on Copenhagen's most prestigious square, where the original building served as a private mansion before becoming Denmark's first luxury hotel. Its Michelin-starred restaurant Marchal occupies the exact spot where royal banquets were once held, and the hotel's wine cellar houses vintages dating back over 100 years.
pro_tip: Book a room facing Kongens Nytorv square for front-row seats to Copenhagen's Christmas market in December, and ask about the secret underground tunnel that once connected the hotel to the Royal Theatre across the square.
dont_miss: The hotel's private balcony suite where Hans Christian Andersen wrote several fairy tales, and the original 18th-century spiral staircase that's still used today. Take afternoon tea in the Palm Court while watching the Changing of the Guard ceremony at nearby Amalienborg Palace.
pros: Prime location on Kongens Nytorv square near Royal Theater and shopping
Historic luxury property with over 260 years of heritage
Exceptional fine dining with Michelin-starred restaurant Marchal
Elegant rooms and suites with classic European luxury design
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects exclusive positioning
Historic building may have smaller room sizes than modern hotels
